title: api_names populated in first pass but collision check in second pass may miss names

finding.claim: api_names populated in first pass but collision check in second pass may miss names
finding.recommendation: Ensure api_names is fully populated before the cross-kind collision check, or restructure to a single pass with deferred validation.

code_region.text:
a suffixed name can never collide with a name another seat owns
    — including a literal agent name like bot-2 meeting the second
    bot seat (v0.7.1 external review, finding 3.1): suffixes keep
    incrementing until the name is unique, and a candidate owned by
    an API seat raises the cross-kind error. Either way, no
    configured seat is ever silently dropped or pooled."""
    parsed = []
    api_names = set()
    for spec in specs:
        if spec.startswith("agent:"):
            base, _options, _cmd = _parse_agent_spec(spec)
            parsed.append(("agent", base, spec))
        elif "|" in spec:
            nm = spec.split("|")[0].strip().lower()
            parsed.append(("api", nm, spec))
            api_names.add(nm)
        else:
            nm = spec.strip().lower()
            parsed.append(("api", nm, spec))
            api_names.add(nm)
    agent_final = {}

refutation.reason: The function performs a full first pass over all specs and adds every API seat name to api_names before the later agent collision loop runs, so the second-pass check does not miss later API names.

probe.summary: Same executed run as packet G10 (`probes/gap_providers_probe.py`, result `gap-providers-cluster.txt`): cross-kind collisions raise ProviderError in **every** spec order (agent-first and API-first, preset and custom forms, case-folded variants), and the no-collision control builds. A name appearing later in the spec list than the agent seat is still caught — the exact "miss" this claim predicts does not occur.
